locator: I q.105 a.5 co., third way, and ad 3: He not only gives things their form, but He also preserves them in existence, and applies them to act
interpretation: Sibling of AQUINAS-ST-I-Q105-A5-EVERY-AGENT-APPLIED-BY-GOD that does not presuppose the name 'God': 'God' is read through the description the article gives, 'the First and Universal Cause', 'properly the cause of universal being which is innermost in all things', i.e. a being that causes the being of every other being. A 'created agent' is an agent other than it whose being it causes; being 'applied to act' is read as being moved in some respect, in the broad sense of motion as reduction from potency to act (prima via); who moves it is not formalized. Cause of being here means giving and preserving esse, not causing a thing's coming to be. This is the premise that rules out an unmoved mover caused in its being, such as a separate intelligence of Aristotle's moving its sphere (result AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-FIRST-MOVER-IS-FIRST-BEING, withoutAppliedAgentNotFirstBeing). Given the quarta via it is close to the identification of the first unmoved mover with the cause of being, which is why its defence matters. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists.
